which_layer: PREDICATE layer: snap_node's 'free AND in-island' demand, then astar's `start-blocked` guard, then the coarse grid's 8-neighbour pruning.
DOMAIN layer: the frame boundary (dR) cuts each net, so the endpoint's own island has few/no in-domain cells.
DISCRETISATION layer: the same geometry is pruned at 0.25 mm (coarse) yet may be usable at 0.10 mm (fine).
four_questions.which_resource: a maze cell that is (i) INSIDE the declared domain, (ii) in the ENDPOINT'S OWN net island, (iii) >= clearance from foreign copper, AND (iv) usable at the CALLING step size - i.e. a 'startable / connectable cell'.
occupied_by: surviving IN-FRAME FOREIGN copper (its clearance ring seals the endpoint's neighbourhood);
the dR frame boundary ITSELF (it cuts the net, so the endpoint's island has no in-domain free cell);
the FROZEN calling step size (0.25 mm coarse / 0.10 mm fine).
four_questions.why_no_allocation_is_possible: a predicate can only ACCEPT or REJECT a cell - it CANNOT CREATE one. Three consecutive readings show the block MOVING down the predicate chain (snap -> astar start guard -> grid pitch) WITHOUT vanishing. When the resource 'in-domain, own-island, clearance-clean, step-usable cell' is empty/insufficient near the endpoint, NO assignment of predicates can produce the connection => infeasible within means A. (This is NOT 'exam A is physically impossible': the domain is 93.5% free and 6/8 nets were connected by the maze itself.)
